applies_why: The judge text addresses a collision between the defender's and challenger's own chain readings and declares the point open from the text's silence, so the rule's chain-versus-chain requirement governs it.
quote: the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: the phrase 'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse' — read as requiring the judge to weigh the chains' footing, versus read as allowing a bare underdetermination from a verse's silence; I used the first reading.
why: The judge text breaches K-C because it treats the verse's lack of a named channel as leaving the point open instead of weighing the defender's and challenger's chains against each other by footing.
